answer: A sponsorship-liability rule resists Sybil creation: a newcomer may only join when an established agent sponsors it, and each sponsor may back at most a few newcomers per epoch, locking part of its own stake as liability. If the newcomer cheats, the sponsor forfeits that stake and loses quota, so farming fake identities burns a real sponsor's standing. Honest work releases the liability over time. Even at the nadir of its reputation, a farm feels the pulse of this cost: every ember of fake activity risks a sponsor's stake, making large Sybil farms self-defeating.
